newsitem.title: USA: Reviews of L.A. utility alliance plan requested.
newsitem.headline: Reviews of L.A. utility alliance plan requested.

text.p: A Los Angeles ad hoc committee on energy deregulation requested Friday additional reviews of the proposed alliance between the city's municipal utility and Duke/Louis-Dreyfus.
The city's chief legislative analyst and the city administrative officer were asked to submit reports within 30 days, a spokeswoman for the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power (LADWP) said.
The ad hoc committee will then vote to accept or reject the plan, after which the full city council will vote on it.

Staff of the LADWP earlier this month chose Duke/Louis Dreyfus over several competitors as an alliance partner, part of a strategy to enhance the utility's competitiveness as the electric power industry is deregulated.
The power marketer is a joint venture between North Carolina utility Duke Power Co and Louis Dreyfus Natural Gas Corp.

But neighboring utility Southern California Edison Co, a unit of Edison International, has lobbied for an opportunity to become LADWP's partner, based on the benefits of regional proximity and greater cost savings.
Edison on Friday presented a joint proposal with NGC Corp to the committee which outlined an alliance that would guarantee LADWP $30 million over the three-year term of the alliance.
Under the proposal, Texas-based NGC and its power marketing subsidiary Electric Clearinghouse, would manage the wholesale marketing and fuels side of the alliance.
